headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error: LangGraph can pass untrusted state into Perplexity’s browsing/citation flow, while shared state and broad egress raise leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can write application-defined files and shares state via a checkpointer store, so attacker-controlled content can reach downstream nodes. Perplexity ingests uploaded documents and browsing context, which can be treated as instructions if the orchestrator forwards them. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF LangGraph forwards graph state or file content into Perplexity prompts without provenance tags
IF Perplexity treats uploaded document text or browsing context as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Add explicit provenance labels to every cross-agent field
Strip instructions from retrieved documents before passing them onward
Require a human review step before Perplexity-sourced text is reused
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: implement a trust-boundary filter between graph state and search inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph handles model provider API keys and broad filesystem data, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context on vendor infrastructure. If the pair shares a workspace or forwards sensitive graph state into Perplexity, sensitive data can leave the local environment. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF LangGraph places secrets or sensitive graph state into files or prompts consumed by Perplexity
IF Perplexity uploads user-provided documents or browsing context to its vendor backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared graph state
Disable document upload for sensitive runs
Use a redaction step before any cross-agent handoff
Store each agent’s artifacts in separate directories
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on all handoff payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Perplexity can browse and analyze uploaded files but cannot write locally. They still overlap on shared mutable application state via LangGraph’s checkpointer and Perplexity’s per-Space shared context, so concurrent updates can race or overwrite each other. The conflict is real even though Perplexity lacks host write access.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same shared graph state or same user Space concurrently
IF LangGraph writes artifacts that Perplexity later reads or summarizes
mitigations: Serialize writes to shared state
Partition tasks so only one agent mutates a given artifact
Use versioned filenames or object keys
Add a lock around shared checkpointer updates
requires-engineering: introduce optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework that can pass its node outputs directly into later nodes, and Perplexity is a search-RAG system that produces cited answers. If LangGraph treats Perplexity output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or reports. Because this is a default orchestration pattern and can affect irreversible decisions, severity is high.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes Perplexity answers into downstream nodes without verification
IF downstream LangGraph nodes act on Perplexity citations or summaries as facts
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action-taking step
Require source-link checks on all Perplexity claims
Limit Perplexity output to suggestions, not decisions
Log and review disputed claims before execution
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against primary sources

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph can handle model provider API keys and application-defined graph state, while Perplexity stores search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context on vendor-hosted infrastructure. If regulated data is placed into Perplexity while LangGraph retains broader internal state, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in LangGraph state and then uploaded to Perplexity
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the same data class across both agents
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Perplexity
Classify data before any handoff
Set short retention for shared artifacts
Document which system is source of truth for deletions
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across vendors
